items.name: Energy sector ETF
items.thesis: Crude is near $98 on Middle East risk, energy led on the hot-CPI day, and Schwab rates Energy 'more favored'. Energy also hedges the inflation risk that hurts the rest of a tech-heavy portfolio.
items.risks: A Mideast de-escalation or a real Russia–Ukraine energy deal could drop crude fast. Demand falls if the Fed over-tightens.
items.trigger: Crude falls back below ~$85, or a durable ceasefire takes the risk premium out.

items.name: Goldman Sachs
items.thesis: Q3 EPS of $17.01 beat consensus by about 30% on record equities trading. Higher-for-longer rates support bank income, and Financials are a favored sector.
items.risks: Trading revenue is cyclical, and the beat is partly priced in after the jump. Credit stress rises if rates keep climbing.
items.trigger: Deal and trading activity slow, or credit spreads widen sharply.

items.name: Gold
items.thesis: Gold is near $4,170 and rising while risk assets fall. Inflation is well above target and the Fed doesn't expect 2% until 2029. A 5–10% position can cushion an inflation or geopolitical shock.
items.risks: Real yields above 5% on the 10-year compete with a non-yielding asset. Gold can pull back sharply after big runs.
items.trigger: Inflation clearly cools and the Fed signals cuts.

items.name: Taiwan Semiconductor
items.thesis: Sixth straight record profit, revenue above guidance, and Q4 guided to $52.3–54.3B. The selloff is about margins, not demand, which can give long-term buyers a better entry.
items.risks: 2nm and overseas fab ramps dilute margins. Taiwan geopolitics. High multiples are sensitive to 5% yields and any AI capex slowdown.
items.trigger: Guidance is cut or big AI customers trim capex plans.

items.name: Nvidia and high-multiple semis
items.thesis: With the 10-year above 5% and hike odds rising, the highest-valuation AI names are being sold first. Memory chips also face new Chinese competition. Trimming an oversized position locks in gains and lowers rate risk.
items.risks: AI earnings keep surprising; Nvidia reports in late November and could reverse the trend. Trimming has tax consequences.
items.trigger: Yields fall back below ~4.75%, or the hot inflation prints prove one-off.

items.name: Short-term Treasuries
items.thesis: With policy at 3.75–4.00% and possibly higher, short T-bills pay close to the policy rate with almost no price risk while you wait for pullbacks.
items.risks: Yields fall if the Fed pivots. You miss upside if stocks rally hard.

items.name: Healthcare sector ETF
items.thesis: Healthcare led European gains and is a favored sector. Its earnings depend less on rates and oil than tech or consumer names.
items.risks: Drug-pricing policy risk. Lags in strong risk-on rallies.
items.trigger: Policy headlines target drug pricing directly.

items.name: Consumer discretionary
items.thesis: Schwab's least-favored sector. $98 oil and higher borrowing costs squeeze spending, and Tesla reports Oct 21 after a 14.5% drop on its last report.
items.risks: A cooling-inflation surprise would rally beaten-down names quickly.
items.trigger: Oil drops sharply or inflation cools.
